title: Both operands of and/or are always evaluated
statement: A logical and or or always evaluates both of its operands, whatever the first one turns out to be.

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict whether a guarded expression raises an error
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts an error from the second operand even though the first operand decides the result

evidence_patterns.item_shape: predict a side effect in the second operand
evidence_patterns.signature: predicts the side effect happens when the first operand already decides the result

example.item:
def f():
    print('called')
    return True
result = False and f()

discriminators.vs_slip: Consistent across items; the learner can state 'it checks both'. A slip is a single wrong prediction.

conflicts_with.label: Logical and/or stop evaluating once the result is known

resolved_by.label: Logical and/or stop evaluating once the result is known
